title: Evolution-Level Quantum Optimal Control of Single-Qubit Gates with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
authors: Yao Du, Jian-Jian Cheng, Lin Zhang, Ming-Liang Hu, Xingang Wang
abstract: Quantum gate design is often represented as pulse optimization, although the physical object that implements a gate is the full controlled evolution generated by the pulse. Here we use physics-informed neural networks to represent single-qubit gate design at this evolution level: the control fields, the Bloch-state trajectories, and the total duration are learned together under the Bloch equation. This changes the optimized object from pulse amplitudes to a differentiable physical process whose structure can be inspected and refined. For rotation gates, the optimized evolutions recover the physical organization expected for bounded single-qubit control, with no prescribed pulse ansatz or duration scan. For a geometric gate, the representation identifies localized bottlenecks in maintaining the geometric condition and turns this diagnosis into feedback, reducing the residual path error while preserving high fidelity. Thus physics-informed learning is used not only to synthesize gates, but also to make optimized quantum controls physically readable, diagnosable, and locally refinable. This process-level view may be especially useful for adapting gates to hardware-specific, task-specific, and locally varying experimental constraints.
summary: This paper pioneers an evolution-level approach to quantum optimal control using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Instead of optimizing pulses, it optimizes the entire controlled dynamical process on the Bloch sphere. This method allows researchers to design gates that are not only high-fidelity but also physically diagnosable and adaptable to complex hardware constraints.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to optimize quantum gate design by treating the entire controlled evolution, rather than just the input pulse amplitudes, as the object of optimization.
main_result: Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) allows for a unified, differentiable framework that optimizes control fields, trajectories, and duration simultaneously, yielding physically readable controls.
method: The authors employ PINNs to encode the Bloch equation dynamics as constraints within the loss function, enabling end-to-end optimization of the quantum process.
model_or_system: The system is a single qubit whose evolution is modeled on the Bloch sphere and governed by a dissipative Bloch vector field ($\dot{\mathbf{r}} = \mathbf{F}[\mathbf{r}, \Omega, \Delta]$).
key_observables: Process fidelity ($	ext{F}_{	ext{proc}}$), average gate fidelity ($	ext{F}_{	ext{avg}}$), and the residual geometric error for path constraints.
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$), optimization weights ($\alpha_{	ext{dyn}},  eta_{	ext{gate}}$), and the trainable duration $T$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the continuous dynamics can be accurately represented by a differentiable function learned via PINNs, which unifies previously separated optimization steps.
figures_summary: Figures compare discrete pulse optimization methods against the proposed PINN generator approach for visualizing control field and trajectory learning.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitation of traditional pulse optimization, proposes the continuous PINN framework to model the full evolution, details the loss function incorporating dynamics and gate requirements, and validates this method on both standard rotation gates and geometrically constrained gates.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, modern computational tool for quantum control that moves beyond simple time-domain pulse shaping by enforcing physical laws directly into the optimization objective, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum hardware protocols.
